title: STRAMP production Stripe is live-mode
context: Production staymtpleasantsc.com was still on Stripe test keys on 2026-09-10. Checkout is fully env-driven; the go-live checklist step to flip the four Stripe env vars had never been done. Todd Gallati could not pay because owners.stripe_customer_id held test-mode customer IDs.
decision: Use Stripe live keys on Vercel production only (preview/local stay on test). Live catalog: STRAMP listing $30/3 months (price_1UECFyGyUu9ML3fKovfbGzNY) and Owner setup fee $50 one-time (price_1UECFyGyUu9ML3fKt3by4Ltr). Live webhook at https://staymtpleasantsc.com/api/stripe/webhook. Null test-mode stripe_customer_id for unpaid owners so live checkout can create live customers. Treat Michelle Whitbeck and Mari Ricozzi as comps: keep subscription_status=active and setup_paid_at, but null their test Stripe IDs. Recreate STRAMPBOARD (100% off forever, max 10) in live mode.
consequences: Todd's next Pay with Stripe is a real $160 charge ($100 setup + $60/quarter).
Approved+paid listings auto-publish via webhook publish_ready_by_customer.
Checkout currently brands as Kneaded.ai (Stripe account display name), not STRAMP.
Amir Fish now has a live $0 STRAMPBOARD subscription used as the webhook smoke test.
Local .env.local and Vercel preview remain on test keys.
alternatives_rejected: Put the 90-day Stripe CLI restricted key (rk_live) in Vercel — it would expire 2026-12-09 and break checkout.
Clear founding-member active status — would unpublish already-live listings that were intended as comps.
Point the live webhook at stramp-platform.vercel.app instead of the canonical domain.

premises.claim: Production checkout is env-driven via STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_PRICE_QUARTERLY, STRIPE_PRICE_SETUP, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
